title: Slice out the first word
description: Write a function `first_word(text)` that returns the first word of `text` (up to the first space), using slicing rather than `.split()`.
hints: Idea to consider: find the space, then slice up to it
text.find(' ') (or text.index(' ')) gives you the position of the first space. A slice text[:position] then takes everything before that position.
Find the index of the first space, then return text sliced from the start up to (not including) that index.
expected_behavior: Returns the substring before the first space.
explanation: find() locates the separator without raising an error if it's missing (unlike index()), and slicing up to that position extracts everything before it in one expression.
